samples.summary: Frontend store's new span and column-width bands have no test, though the same describe block argues they need one
samples.evidence: The new describe 'bands the numeric attributes a peer can write' (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts ~3380-3500) covers fontSize, image size, cell padding, rowHeights and listLevel. It does not cover the two bands this diff also wires into the *same* parser: `normalizeTableSpan` on colSpan/rowSpan (src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:460-461) and `parseColumnWidthsAttr` on the `cols` attribute (line ~476). The block's own preamble says this parser is a duplicate of crdt-tree.ts with 'no shared test', and that 'the frontend has no tsc lane to catch a band wired to the wrong field' — which is exactly the risk left uncovered here. The span band is the one guarding `expandCellRangeForMerges`' non-terminating loop (a permanently hung tab), and the frontend copy is the one live collaborators run. The test is feasible: colSpan/rowSpan are serialized as attribute strings (yorkie-doc-store.ts:255-256, applyCellSpan at 2743) exactly like the rowHeights case that is tested.
searchedFor: read the new describe block in the diff

samples.summary: sanitizeDocStyles wiring at both CRDT read boundaries is untested (only the pure function is)
samples.evidence: `sanitizeDocStyles` itself is well covered in packages/docs/test/model/named-styles.test.ts, but neither call site is: `YorkieDocStore.getDocStyles()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts ~705) has no test (grep for `getDocStyles`/`stylesJson` in packages/frontend/tests finds none), and `docsTreeToDocument`'s `doc.styles = sanitizeDocStyles(JSON.parse(...))` has no test in packages/docs/test (grep 'stylesJson|docsTreeToDocument' there returns no matches). The only adjacent coverage is snapshot-adapters.test.ts, which asserts an unknown key passes through — that assertion holds with or without the sanitizer. So a registry-level poisoned fontSize/lineHeight (the stated document-wide bypass) is never asserted to be banded at either boundary.

samples.summary: Slides band: colSpan branch, the MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS count cap, the lineHeight drop branch and the notes path are untested
samples.evidence: The new spec (docs-content.controller.spec.ts:1824-1928) covers inline fontSize clamp+drop, block lineHeight clamp, listLevel, rowHeights, columnWidths magnitude, cell padding and `rowSpan: Infinity`. Untested in `bandSlideBlockNumerics`/`bandSlideCellNumerics`: the `colSpan` half of the span loop (only rowSpan is exercised), the `.slice(0, MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS)` count cap on columnWidths (only magnitude is asserted), the `delete record.lineHeight` drop branch (e.g. lineHeight 0/-1), and the fact that `assertValidSlideBlocks` — hence the banding — also runs over a slide's `notes` blocks. Each failure is a value stored verbatim in a deck and rendered by every viewer.
searchedFor: read the whole new describe block in the diff

samples.summary: Repair-not-reject contract (the PUT echo / GET→edit→PUT round trip) is only asserted against the exported helper, never through the endpoint
samples.evidence: The new tests call `assertValidSlidesBody(deck)` directly and inspect the mutated object. The doc comment's central claim — the endpoint 'echoes the same object back' so what the caller sees is what is stored, and a GET→edit→PUT of a deck already holding an out-of-band value keeps working — is never exercised through the controller's PUT path (no test asserts the response body or the value handed to `writeSlidesRoot` carries the banded numbers). A regression where the controller validates a clone, or persists the pre-band body, would pass.
searchedFor: read controller PUT path lines 195, 266 references

samples.summary: pdf-painter's two new normalizeListLevel call sites have no test
samples.evidence: pdf-painter.ts:367 and :593 now normalize `block.listLevel` before multiplying it into the marker x / using it as a counter key. No test in packages/docs/test/export exercises a poisoned level through the PDF painter (grep 'listLevel' there hits only with-list.json and the exporter tests, which use ordinary levels). The comment in editor-tab-bullet.test.ts explicitly defers these call sites to the band's own unit test, which cannot catch a call site that was left un-normalized or normalized in the wrong place (e.g. the marker x computed from the raw level). Same applies to table-renderer.ts:525 and peer-cursor.ts:255/395.
searchedFor: read list-level.test.ts coverage list in the diff

samples.summary: Two of the three 'poisoned value neither hangs nor floods pages' loops assert a bound that is satisfied trivially
samples.evidence: In `paginateCellWith` tests, the Infinity and NaN cases now flow through computeTableLayout step 5d, which substitutes MIN_ROW_HEIGHT, so the result is a single page and `expect(result.pages.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(202)` holds regardless of MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN or of the numeric bands under test. Only the finite `1e9` case discriminates (without the paginator bound it would build ~1.1M pages). The Infinity/NaN iterations are effectively termination smoke tests; they would stay green if the band and the bound were both removed, provided step 5d remains. Asserting the actual page count / row height for those inputs would make them discriminating.
searchedFor: read paginateCellWith tests in the diff

samples.summary: The `if (!(fragHeight > 0)) fragHeight = remaining;` floor is acknowledged unreachable and has no test
samples.evidence: pagination.ts:164-170 documents the line as 'unreachable today (verified by making it throw against the whole suite)'. It is therefore dead code no test can cover; the table-row-split.test.ts case that mentions it explicitly says it takes the `fragHeight = remaining` default instead. Noting only so the untestable branch is visible, not as a blocker.

verdict.reason: The frontend read boundary's span and column-width bands are genuinely untested in the frontend package. The new describe block (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3372-3499) covers only fontSize (3406), image size (3424), cell padding (3440), rowHeights (3456) and listLevel (3477); no test feeds a hostile colSpan/rowSpan or cols attribute through a peer read. I searched the whole frontend package: normalizeTableSpan|parseColumnWidthsAttr|MAX_TABLE_SPAN|MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS appear only in src/, never in tests/, and Infinity|1e400|1e9 across packages/frontend/tests hits only the five banded fields plus unrelated files. The existing span tests (2719-2945) use well-formed values via applyCellSpan and read back from the writing store, which answers from cachedDoc (src 667-669, 1529), so they never run treeNodeToRow; columnWidths is asserted only same-store (test 1250) or as happy-path convergence (concurrent integration:866) - neither fails if a band is removed. Mitigation I did find: packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts:246-329 tests both band functions with Infinity/1e9/1e400/count-cap, tests the docs-package read boundary via treeNodeToBlock, and pins the expandCellRangeForMerges non-termination regression; the frontend imports the same helpers from @wafflebase/docs (src 55-56), so the band logic itself cannot drift. That makes the finding's quoted premise 'no shared test' inaccurate about the helpers, but it is not a counterexample to the claim filed: nothing executes the frontend call sites at src 460-461 and 480, so a band dropped or wired to the wrong field in the copy live collaborators run (no tsc lane there) ships green, with a permanently hung tab as the user-visible failure. Real, uncovered guard - stays on the gate.
